stem: (Select TWO.) Orchard Health's nightly job runs `terraform apply -state=ci.tfstate -backup=ci.bak` on the local backend. After a trial of an S3 backend, the team is considering deleting the backend block again. Which two statements are correct?

choices.text: Those options are legacy features kept for backward compatibility, and the docs no longer recommend them for new systems
The docs recommend those options as the standard way to point automation at a shared remote state location
Once the configuration names an S3 backend, the same options keep working and override the bucket location
Deleting the backend block and re-running `terraform init` prompts Terraform to offer migrating the state to the default local backend
Deleting the backend block makes the next `terraform init` discard the stored state, because local is treated as a fresh start

rationale: `-state`, `-state-out` and `-backup` are legacy local-backend options preserved for backward compatibility; the docs recommend choosing a backend that supports remote state instead, so presenting them as the recommended shared-state method is wrong. They have no effect when a different backend type is selected, so they cannot override a bucket location. Removing the backend block and reinitializing leads Terraform to prompt about migrating the state to the default local backend, so nothing is discarded as a fresh start.
